entities.name: Hillel the Elder
entities.label: Person
entities.summary: One of the most important figures in Jewish history (c. 110 BCE – 10 CE), a Babylonian-born scholar who became president of the Sanhedrin in Jerusalem. Famous for summarizing the Torah: "What is hateful to you, do not do to your fellow. That is the whole Torah; the rest is commentary. Go and study." Hillel established seven hermeneutical rules (middot) for interpreting Scripture that became foundational for rabbinic exegesis. His school (Beit Hillel), generally more lenient than the rival Beit Shammai, won most halakhic disputes and shaped mainstream Rabbinical Judaism. His descendants held the patriarchate for 400+ years.
